ending.verdict: You traded the open workshop for unbroken dinners and a safe margin, and your family always knew when you were coming home.

branchVerdicts.b-d-42-1-c: Harder physical days and leaner initial margins gave your parents your daily presence and gave your hands real cedar to shape.
branchVerdicts.b-d-46-1-b: You waited until the kids were grounded before stepping out, paying for the late start with sore joints and earning an honest craft.
branchVerdicts.b-d-58-1-b: You waited out every corporate duty until the safety was total, then filled your seventies with cedar shavings and young apprentices.

fiveYear.chosen: In five years I see myself working a predictable schedule in QA documentation so I can be home for dinner by six. I want to make sure Haruto finishes his middle school terms without unnecessary upheaval, and I plan to attend every one of Mei's recitals. On weekends, I will keep building simple furniture on our balcony and taking the express bus to check on my parents in Kochi.
fiveYear.b-d-42-1-c: In five years I see myself running a modest, solvent woodworking shop near the river in Kochi. I want our family settled in a house where my parents have direct daily support as they grow older. It will be a major adjustment after nineteen years in Osaka electronics, but I expect to have my first line of handmade tables completed and a sustainable local clientele.
fiveYear.b-d-46-1-b: In five years I see myself managing a small furniture workshop in Kochi, taking custom orders for regional cedar furniture. Having Haruto settled into high school gives me the room to step away from corporate QA and be physically close to my father while his health needs attention. I expect the income will be tighter, but I will be doing tangible work with wood every day.
fiveYear.b-d-58-1-b: In five years I see myself running an independent wood studio near Tennoji, keeping the doors open for custom joinery and small weekend classes. The corporate pension gives us the security we need, so the shop can focus on quality rather than rapid volume. I want to spend my mornings turning wood on a real lathe and my afternoons teaching people how to care for hand tools.

transcript.chat: I wish I'd known that the exhaustion wasn't permanent, but it wouldn't fix itself without giving something up. Taking the pay cut and stepping down into documentation gave me my evenings back, and dinner at six with the kids was worth every yen we didn't save. I also wish I'd known that you don't need a real commercial studio to be a craftsman. The balcony is cramped and the neighbors hear the planer, but the cedar smells just as good out there.
